Rumo inalterado

Statement indicating that the vessel’s heading remains as previously instructed or reported.

Quick answer: Statement indicating that the vessel’s heading remains as previously instructed or reported.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Rumo inalterado?

In this glossary, Rumo inalterado refers to: Statement indicating that the vessel’s heading remains as previously instructed or reported.

How is Rumo inalterado used in maritime?

In maritime communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "MV Orion, rumo inalterado, seguindo pela rota designada, solicito confirmação do tráfego."

Why does Rumo inalterado matter in maritime?

Rumo inalterado matters because it supports clear communication in External Communication contexts for Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as STCW, Marlins Test, ISF Watchkeeper, and GMDSS.

Who uses Rumo inalterado?

Rumo inalterado is mainly used by Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters.

What category does Rumo inalterado belong to?

In this glossary, Rumo inalterado is grouped under External Communication. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from IMO SMCP, STCW Convention, SOLAS, COLREG and published by Protermify Maritime as a static maritime reference page.

Definition

Statement indicating that the vessel’s heading remains as previously instructed or reported.

Operational example

MV Orion, course unchanged, proceeding along assigned track, request traffic confirmation.

Localized term

Rumo inalterado

Localized example

MV Orion, rumo inalterado, seguindo pela rota designada, solicito confirmação do tráfego.
